---
title: Save a list as a view
description: Save a query, a sort and a grouping as a view, so every app lists the same items the same way, then change, delete or read it.
---

A [view](/catalog/view) saves a listing so every app shows the same one. Its `query` says which items it lists, and its `sort` and `group` say in what order and how they group. **How an app shows the items is the app's own**, so a view holds no layout.

## Create a view

[Create a view](/api-reference/views/createView) with a `title`. Optionally add a `query` of `types`, `tier`, `state`, `filter` and `beneath`, a `sort` of `by` and `direction` keys, and a `group` with a `by` field:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa views create --title "Open tasks" \
  --query '{"types":["core.task"],"filter":"properties.status neq \"completed\""}' \
  --sort '[{"by":"updated_at","direction":"desc"}]' \
  --group '{"by":"properties.priority"}'
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /views
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "title": "Open tasks",
  "query": { "types": ["core.task"], "filter": "properties.status neq \"completed\"" },
  "sort": [{ "by": "updated_at", "direction": "desc" }],
  "group": { "by": "properties.priority" }
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.POST("/views", {
  body: {
    title: "Open tasks",
    query: { types: ["core.task"], filter: 'properties.status neq "completed"' },
    sort: [{ by: "updated_at", direction: "desc" }],
    group: { by: "properties.priority" },
  },
});
```

In the TypeScript example, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows.

The answer is the view as a `system.view` item at `version` 1. The server returns its settings, not the items it lists. **The device core can read its items and groups offline**, as [Read a view offline](/build/read-a-view) shows.

A view's `filter` takes any expression that [List, filter and search](/build/list-filter-search#filter-by-properties) describes, so a view can list one folder's items with `edge[in-folder] eq "<folder id>"`, or one source's with `source eq "<source>"`.

## Change, delete or read a view

- **To change a view,** [update it](/api-reference/views/updateView) with the `version` you read and the settings you change. Each one you name is replaced whole, and a change based on an older version still applies when nobody changed the same setting since. To stop a view grouping its items, send `group: null`, or run `marfa views change <id> --version <n> --group null`; the change is to the `group` setting alone, so it follows the same rule.
- **To delete a view,** [delete it](/api-reference/views/deleteView). It's gone at once, with no trash.
- **To read a view,** [get it](/api-reference/items/getItem) by its `id`, or list the type `system.view`, like any other item.

## What your key needs

Writing a view needs write on `system.view`, and reading one needs read; a `content:*` scope reaches neither. Marfa refuses a malformed setting before it writes anything, and names it in `details.errors[0].path`, such as `group.bucket`. The rules are in the [views](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/views.md) chapter of the contract.
